What does it take to climb out of the trash and into the sky?

The very heavens had decreed his death. He should have died in the womb. Or in infancy. Or when his family was murdered. Or when the house burned around him. Or when he woke up in the dump suffering from innumerable diseases and missing fingers. Even the magic ring with a ghostly grandpa trapped inside of it was sabotaged. A reasonable person would roll over and die. Tian isn't that reasonable. And as it happens, neither is Grandpa Jun. In a world where immortality can be cultivated, miracles are things you make for yourself. A broken boy will defy the heavens, and soar.

Love can make you lose your head.

Seth il Gutierre is a thief with bad habits and worse luck. He has one chance to clear his debt: steal from a deadly warrior with black eyes and a soul-drinking sword.

Annalise al Ydris is a Verdugo, a traveling executioner of the Sorcerer General’s legion who must spill enough blood to fuel the ancient necromancy holding the seraph hordes at bay. When she catches Seth, he’s sure his head is forfeit and his soul will be fuel for the deathspell.

Instead, she gives him a job.

Now he’s Annalise’s personal thief, helping her carve her tithe from the enemies plaguing the last surviving continent. Seth must survive monsters, madmen, and the strange, simmering desire building between him and the cheerful headtaker he serves.

Headless Over Heels is a romance in a 1920s-inflected dark fantasy setting, about the healing power of love and the harming power of massive necromantic greatswords.

Lost and Found: Living as a Relic of Ages Past. Aboard a Grand Cruiser once lost now owned by a Rogue Trader dynasty with a heavy Adeptus Mechanicus presence. A soul wakes up shortly after the formation of the Cicatrix Maledictum, in a new unfamiliar body with a diverse suite of implants from the dark age.

Primarily and originally uploaded on Spacebattles under my same username.

Hello. This is my first writing project that I've posted here. It's a personal passion project that has been in the works for over a year now.
It will include a mixture of first person pov segments from the SI and third person segments of other pertinent characters to give broader context. Feedback is appreciated. I apologize for my grammar in advance, remembering commas is hard.

Overall the vibes I was going for were to show what a competent and well equipped group could do when cut off and tossed near the edge of known space, mixed with 40k space ship slice of life, a bit of gear/ship/tech binging and of course typical 40k awful shenanigans. No crossover abilities just a bit of external lore to help guide the SI.

I draw a lot on bits of lore and items from the fantasy flight tabletop rpg games, and a bit from the novels, the regular tabletop and video games.

Italics will be used for Noosphere, Vox, and digital communications and ship names.

This content is only posted to Royalroad and cross posted to Spacebattles for free.

Disclaimer: Warhammer 40,000 and all associated characters, names, and lore are the sole property of Games Workshop. This is a work of fanfiction and no copyright infringement is intended. Original characters and plotlines are my own.

A hundred tries to get it right. No more, no less.

For twenty years, Balzam Magnos terrorized the world as its third Overlord: conquering kingdoms, slaughtering heroes, and crushing rebels under his iron boot. None could stand up to him. 

But then he died, and Simon is now stuck with his Class. 

Owning the most powerful Class in the world has its downsides. The paladins? They want his head. His overpowered siblings? They want his throne. His empress stepmother? She wants both. And his predecessor’s assassin is still out there.

But the Overlord Class has a secret: its user can turn back time to their coronation up to a hundred times, reliving their reigns until death. 

Simon has a hundred reigns to grow strong enough to fulfill his dreams. Not one more, not one less.

Better make each one count.

Cover art done by Tofuyi!

BOOK 1 COMPLETED! 

The war ended, but the world didn't. 

For years, the lands burned in the wars of the White Queen, a sorceress and tyrant whose mad ambition brought ruin to all she touched. Now she is dead, but all that remains has been bled dry. Charred towns lie hollow, fields return to the wild, and quiet shadows settle where folk once made their homes. The gods themselves seem tired. Where humanity retreats, darkness creeps in. 

Through this darkness the young wizard Martimeos walks the broken roads, following the fading trail of his brother, who marched west to fight in the Queen's War and never returned. He left behind no grave, no message, no certainty. Only rumors of what he'd done. 

On his journey Martimeos must barter with demons, trade riddles with fae, and contend with the wild witch Elyse, a fellow practitioner of the Art with secrets of her own. At last the road brings him to Silverfish, a cursed village whose future has been stolen, overgrown with thorns and lies. His search will lead him to the horror at the heart of Silverfish's tragedy—and the truth behind his brother's fate. 

WANDER WEST, IN SHADOW is a dark fantasy set in a world of faded kingdoms and lost history, with no litrpg elements. Magic is subtle, especially when Elyse and Martimeos first set out, and it is often better to run than it is to stand and fight.

After years of exile, Marcus is coming back home. A powerful mage with few equals, Marcus lives in a world full of monsters and powerful adepts, many of which have bad histories with him. But he has not come back to pursue vengeance or start a fight. All Marcus wants to do is reconnect with old friends, build himself a house, and maybe train a successor or two.

Zenith of Sorcery is set in its own original setting and isn’t related to Mother of Learning… beyond being written by the same person, of course. Protect my sister.

That’s all that ever mattered to me. Come hell or high water, I’d do anything if it meant my sweet little sister could have just one more day of a peaceful life. Anything. 

There was just one issue—I was burning the candle at both ends. Between my double-life as a villainous Anarch and a member of the heroic Guardians, my days were becoming more and more chaotic. That wasn’t even the worst part. I hadn’t gotten to the anomalies yet.

Every day was a balancing act just to keep breathing. Lying to my friends, hunting monsters, and keeping my sister smiling—it was tiring enough just trying to fall asleep, let alone everything else. I didn’t have a choice, though. Never really did. If I played my cards just right, a better life might just be in sight.

To survive as an alien tyrant's husband, he'll need to grab his new life by the horns.

A late shift watching an empty cell in a middle-of-nowhere facility? Sign Grant up. If the money's good, he'll gladly take the peace and quiet of a long, boring night.

And then he meets the prisoner: Subject B-31. Blue, beautiful, and inhuman.

He's told to think of her as a test subject, not a person. He's told to ignore the sorrow on her face and the desperation in her crimson eyes. Maybe he should have listened. Because his rescue attempt quickly turns into an alien abduction.

B-31 is Sykora, a princess of the tyrannical Taiikari Empire, who whisks Grant into a galaxy filled with alien cultures, deadly rivals, and the sinister smiles of the Taiikari royal court. Grant will have to learn a new life, and learn it fast.

Because when the Princess of the Void looks at Grant, she doesn't just see a savior—she sees a husband.

And she isn't asking.

What to expect: Fun and satire, and eventually some darker parts.

Notorious internet troll and critic, Amy Stake, has "karma" catch up to her when she criticizes the writing of a vengeful Goddess and gets reincarnated into a brutal shonen battle manga known for its astronomical body count.

In an ironic twist of fate, she'll only get the powers the manga readers imagine she has, and her strength will be directly proportional to how much they love her.

With death lurking at every step, Amy must now claw her way into the main story by any means necessary. Scene-stealing entrances, manufactured drama, and a possibly fabricated tragic backstory… Whatever it takes to secure her place as a fan favorite before the end of the world arrives.
